tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly: rank 7 > 3, and three conditioning ingredients precede the marker (Stearyl Alcohol @2, Stearamidopropyl Dimethylamine @3, Cetyl Alcohol @4). The marker is early relative to a 23-entry list, so Behentrimonium Methosulfate @11, Panthenol @15, Panthenyl Ethyl Ether @16, Histidine @18 and Biotin @22 are all demoted. That demotion is well-founded here: this is a genuinely short-payload formula, not a hero-tail artefact.  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): PLAUSIBLE. STEARYL ALCOHOL @2, STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @3, CETYL ALCOHOL @4 and BIS-AMINOPROPYL DIMETHICONE @5 - the complete credited architecture - outrank PARFUM @7; conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA @1. BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @11 sits below the marker, an ordinary single-species demotion in a genuinely short-payload formula. GLUTAMIC ACID @6 is the tail_index - 1 species; it is the amidoamine neutraliser (lexicon C3) and carries no signal in any field, so R3's tail-edge exclusion changes nothing here.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, exact-market DE INCI of record (sha256 7be31024…, direct Müller fetch), above-tail ranks 1–6; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Exactly one of the three §9.1 structural signals is satisfied, which §9.1 assigns to the moderate bucket by definition. This is a structurally minimal formula: one cationic species, two fatty alcohols, one silicone, no lipid. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: STEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three, the one satisfied signal
STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE (rank 3) — the only cationic species above the tail
BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE (rank 11) — a second cationic, but BELOW tail_index 7
no non-fatty-alcohol lipid at any rank above the tail (Bis-Aminopropyl Dimethicone @5 is an R2 silicone, not an R4 lipid; Glutamic Acid @6 is a free amino acid)
CETYL ALCOHOL (rank 4) — a second fatty alcohol, but S2 asks for rank 2 or 3, which Stearyl Alcohol already satisfies; breadth of fatty alcohols is not a separate signal
conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 (≥2 distinct cationics above the tail) = NOT satisfied; one. S2 satisfied (Stearyl Alcohol @2). S3 (≥2 distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail) = NOT satisfied; zero. Count = 1 of 3.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: §9.1 assigns `moderate` to 'everything else, including exactly one satisfied signal'. Exactly one is satisfied.
`high` does not apply: it requires ≥2 of {S1,S2,S3}. Only S2 holds, and the second cationic that would have carried S1 sits four ranks below the marker.

`low` does not apply: it requires NONE of the three — specifically a single cationic species AND no fatty alcohol in the top three AND at most one lipid above the tail. The first and third conditions hold, but Stearyl Alcohol @2 defeats the second.

Confidence is `moderate` rather than `high` by the §9.1 rule itself: high confidence requires ≥2 signals pointing the same way, and only one is available — despite this being the cohort's best-sourced formula.

Re-derived under v0.2 (R3): the value `moderate` STANDS, and the route to it is unchanged in substance. S1 fails — STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @3 is the only cationic above the tail, and BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @11 is tail-side. S2 is satisfied by STEARYL ALCOHOL @2. S3 fails: there is no lipid of any class above the tail. One signal, and S1 is not it, so `high` is doubly unreachable. The tail-edge exclusion changes nothing: the tail_index − 1 species is GLUTAMIC ACID @6, which carries no structural signal. No material counter-signal fires.
counterSignals: Polysorbate 20 @13, Disodium EDTA @12 and Methicone @23 are formulation infrastructure in the tail and earn nothing (lexicon family 10).
Biotin @22 earns zero credit on every property and is kept away from any hair-loss-adjacent language (G6).
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support.
This is the one cohort product where source quality is excellent and the signal count is still thin — the scale's resolution, not the evidence, is the limit.

thresholdReasoning: Clears `smoothing`: step 6 requires dry surface control to be the clearest practical differentiator AND the architecture to extend materially beyond the ordinary mask base via a distinct silicone, substantive polymer, or substantial lipid route. The amino silicone at rank 5 is the only thing in this formula that is not base, so it is by construction both the clearest differentiator and the material extension.

`repair` does not apply, and this is the product's whole purpose in the cohort: the strongest bond positioning in the set produces no repair focus, because step 3 names 'generic repair naming' and 'bond_specific_support = claim_only' as things that cannot set `repair`.

`general` was the close competitor and lost narrowly. The argument that won: §9.5.1 explicitly routes a `nonspecific` verdict to `smoothing` when the dry-surface route genuinely clears step 6, and an amino silicone at rank 5 of 6 above-tail entries is a real, distinct, non-baseline route. adjudicationPoints.title: The cohort's only `balanced` / `neither_dominant` value — and it is not the product R6 was written around — ESCALATION
adjudicationPoints.body: R6's reading (b) was drafted with the structurally minimal gloss mask in mind, and the standard names L'Oréal Elsève Glycolic Gloss as its anchor case. On this cohort it fires on a different product entirely. Pantene Molecular Bond Repair's credited segment is AQUA @1, STEARYL ALCOHOL @2, STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @3, CETYL ALCOHOL @4, BIS-AMINOPROPYL DIMETHICONE @5, GLUTAMIC ACID @6 — a bare R1 base plus one amino silicone, with zero humectants and zero lipids above the tail. Clause 1 holds (no protein at any rank), clause 2 holds (the silicone is the only species beyond the baseline), clause 3 holds (nothing above the tail beyond the bare R1 baseline), clause 4 holds vacuously (there is no candidate leg species to outrank). So the value is `balanced` / `neither_dominant`, moving from v0.1's `moisture` at `high` confidence. Meanwhile #11, the anchor case, FAILS clause 4 — its single humectant PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5 outranks the AMODIMETHICONE @6 that establishes clause 2 — and keeps `moisture`. Two things for Nick. First, is a single amino silicone a 'substantive R2 silicone system' for clause 2? If not, this value returns to `moisture` and reading (b) is reached nowhere in the cohort. Second, clause 4's vacuous satisfaction on a formula with no legs at all is arguably the cleanest possible case for reading (b), yet it reads as a technicality; whereas on the anchor case clause 4 blocks the reading on a one-rank difference between a glycol and a silicone. §18 open question 4 asks how often reading (b) is reachable; this run's answer is 'once, and not where expected'.
